Mateszalka New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Arad utca 6, Hungary

Not demolished. This is the newer of two Jewish cemeteries in Mátészalka, established in the second half of the 20th century — its oldest gravestone dates to 1964. Mátészalka's Jewish community, first recorded in 1784-85, grew to 1,621 people by 1930; the actor Tony Curtis, whose family came from the town, made a significant donation toward renovating the exterior of its synagogue during a visit, and a plaque on the building's wall commemorates Adolf Zukor, founder of Paramount Pictures, who lived in Mátészalka between 1881 and 1885. About 17,000 Jews, including those from the wider Máramaros district, were confined in the Mátészalka Ghetto before deportation to Auschwitz.
